title: Sarkozy brokers a ceasefire agreement between Russia and Georgia
body:
On 12 August 2008 French President Nicolas Sarkozy, who held the rotating presidency of the European Union, travelled between Moscow and Tbilisi to broker an end to the fighting. After meeting Russian President Dmitry Medvedev in Moscow, Sarkozy met Georgian President Mikheil Saakashvili, and the two agreed a modified version of the peace plan agreed with Russia. Saakashvili called it "an agreement of principles".

Medvedev ordered a halt to military operations in Georgia and supported the plan Sarkozy promoted. The changes Medvedev approved included removing a reference to talks on the future status of South Ossetia. The joint text laid down six conditions for a lasting settlement. Both sides declared a ceasefire, but each accused the other of failing to keep its promises: Georgia said Russian jets were bombing two villages outside South Ossetia, and Russia's Defence Ministry called this an "information provocation" and said Georgian guns kept firing on its positions.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Georgia must withdraw its troops well beyond South Ossetia's borders and sign a legally binding pledge not to attack again. US envoy Matthew Bryza called the Russian move "extremely positive". Georgia also said it was leaving the Commonwealth of Independent States. The UN estimated that more than 100,000 people had been displaced, according to RTE's report.
